transcript.text: Let me check if there are any SailPoint-specific tools available for this.

This is a standard **OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant**. Send your `client_id` and `client_secret` in the **POST body** (never in the URL) to your tenant's `/oauth/token` endpoint.

## Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Replace `{tenant}` with your ISC tenant name (e.g. `acme` → `acme.api.identitynow.com`).

## Example with curl

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  --data-urlencode "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
  --data-urlencode "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"
```

## Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 750
}
```

## Using the token

Pass it as a bearer token on every subsequent API call:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5...
```

> **Note for `beta` endpoints:** Also add the header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`.

## Key points

- Credentials go in the **body**, never in the query string — doing otherwise exposes secrets in server logs and browser history.
- Tokens expire in ~12.5 minutes (`expires_in: 750` seconds); request a new one when it expires.
- Rate limit is **100 requests per token per 10 seconds**. A `429` response includes a `Retry-After` header — respect it before retrying.
- PATs are capped at **10 per user** across your tenant.

---

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: POST
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth
auth_flow: OAuth2 client credentials grant
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [grant_type, client_id, client_secret]
```
